title: If justified before conversion: absurd—death/life and love collapse
source_text: XVII. Adde quod, si dicamus justificationem esse aliquid vocatione prius, & electos, non tantum in divino decreto, sed actu & reipsa justificatos esse, priusquam in Christum credant, & convertantur, multa sequuntur absurda, & quae Apostolicae doctrinae plane adversantur. Nam qui justificatus est, & remissionem peccatorum suorum a Deo consecutus, transit a morte ad vitam, nec amplius in morte manet. Qui vero nondum est ad Deum conversus, adhuc in morte manet; quandoquidem, nec Deum, nec proximum vera charitate diligit. Nam ut affirmat Joannes, Qui non diligit fratrem manet in morte, 1 Joh. 3. 14. Posita autem illa, quam refutamus, hypothesi, vel necesse est aliquem, qui justificatus est, in morte adhuc manere, nec transiisse de morte ad vitam: vel, contra expressum Apostoli dictum, aliquem nec proximum, nec Deum diligere, & in morte tamen non manere.
pass_a_gloss: Add that if we say justification is something prior to calling, and that the elect are not only in the divine decree but actually and in reality justified before they believe in Christ and are converted, many absurdities follow that plainly oppose apostolic doctrine. For whoever is justified and has obtained remission of his sins from God passes from death to life and no longer remains in death. But whoever is not yet converted to God still remains in death; since he loves neither God nor neighbor with true charity. For as John affirms, Whoever does not love his brother remains in death (1 John 3:14). But given the hypothesis we refute, either it is necessary that someone who is justified still remain in death and not have passed from death to life; or, against the Apostle's express word, that someone love neither neighbor nor God and yet not remain in death.
pass_b_english: Actual justification before conversion yields absurdities against the apostles.
Justified = passed from death to life; unconverted lovelessness still 'remains in death.'
